about: The contract for POST /v0/plan (#277), recorded: one case per rule the planner
answers by, and the exact batch it has to answer with.
AL.1 implements this contract with a deterministic outline parser and AN.1 (#289)
implements the SAME contract with a real planner once the invocation gateway
exists. The `response` bodies here are outline-v0's and are asserted verbatim by
ouroboros-engine's tests/test_planning_golden.py. What AN.1 inherits is the
SHAPE -- v0.json beside this file -- not these values: a planner that decomposes
a narrative properly will answer `narrative-only` with several drafts, and that is
the point of it. A case's `planner` field is therefore part of the recording too.
Determinism is the property this file exists to pin. The same request produces the
same batch, the same local keys and the same notes in the same order, in every
process -- which is what makes a regenerate that CHANGED something meaningful.
Regenerating this file is not how it is maintained. It is reviewed and frozen; a
change to it is a change to the contract.

cases.name: ota-outline
cases.about: The mockup's own outcome and an outline for it: six drafts carrying mockup 09's dependency shape and workflow tags, and nothing to explain.

request.narrative: We need OTA updates to survive power loss mid-flash: staged A/B partitions, checksum verification before swap, automatic rollback, and a recovery beacon over BLE if both slots are bad.
request.outline:
- Partition table & bootloader slot flag for A/B scheme  blocks: OTA-3
  - two slots, with the active one named in the bootloader header
  - fall back to the previous slot when the flag is unset
- SHA-256 checksum verification before slot swap  blocks: OTA-3
  - verify the staged image before the swap, never after it
- Rollback state machine on failed boot confirmation  blocks: OTA-5
  - restore the previous slot
  - emit a telemetry event
- BLE recovery beacon when both slots fail checksum  blocks: OTA-5
  - advertise a recovery service when neither slot verifies
- Power-loss integration tests on HIL rig (kill power mid-flash)  [hil-verify]
  - cut power during erase, during write, and during the swap
- Operator docs: recovery procedure & beacon pairing  [docs]

cases.name: numbered-sequence
cases.about: A numbered list is somebody writing down an order, so each item depends on the one before it -- and the plan discloses that it drew those edges.

request.outline:
1. Stand up the provisioning service
2. Migrate the first cohort
3. Cut over the remaining fleet

notes: Numbered items are read as a sequence: each depends on the one before it. Use `-` bullets for work that can run in parallel.

cases.name: after-annotation
cases.about: `after:` is the same edge written from the other end, and an unordered list gets no edges it was not given.

cases.name: ignored-and-explained
cases.about: Everything this planner will not invent, in one batch: a marker no workflow matches, a dependency on a key that is not in the batch, an annotation indented under a bullet, and prose before the first one. Each is ignored and each produces a note.

notes: Ignored dependency annotations naming keys that are not in this batch: HRD-9. Keys are assigned by position, so the third bullet is the third key.
Ignored workflow markers that match no workflow this installation has: [security-sweep].
`blocks:` and `after:` are read from a bullet's own line. 1 indented line(s) carrying one were kept as body text instead.
1 line(s) before the first bullet are not part of any ticket. Describe the outcome in the narrative and keep the outline to a list.
